# Cyclop

> A free, open-source macOS utility that turns the MacBook notch into a panel:
> media controls, a file shelf, clipboard history, snippets, the next meeting,
> offline translation, a currency converter, a teleprompter, scratch notes and
> a keyboard lock for cleaning. Native SwiftUI and AppKit, no third-party
> dependencies, MIT licence.

Cyclop is invisible at rest. Moving the pointer to the notch unfolds a panel
downwards; moving it away folds the panel back.

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 15 or newer, Apple silicon only (releases are arm64)
- Licence: MIT, free, no paid tier, no subscription, no accounts
- Bundle size: 3.7 MB. Memory: about 40 MB plus a 14 MB helper. 0.0% CPU at rest
- Dependencies: none. Swift, SwiftUI and AppKit only
- The promise: nothing at launch. Two permissions, each asked only on a button
  press, after an explanation: Calendar and Accessibility. The only network
  traffic is currency rates and, on the fallback path, Spotify artwork. 0 % CPU
  at rest
- Permissions: nothing is asked at launch. Calendar is for the Calendar tab;
  Accessibility is for the keyboard and trackpad cleaning lock in the Utilities
  tab. Each is requested only by an explicit button press on a screen that
  explains why. A tab switched off in Settings never asks for its permission.
  No Screen Recording in any mode. The fallback player path, used only if the
  main one stops working, would also need Automation for Apple Music and
  Spotify. A file placed on the shelf from Downloads, Documents or the Desktop
  is asked about separately by macOS, when the shelf is opened
- Network: no telemetry and no analytics. Currency rates for the Currency tab,
  once an hour from cdn.jsdelivr.net (fallback: latest.currency-api.pages.dev),
  only while that tab is enabled. On the fallback player path only, Spotify
  album artwork, from the image URL Spotify provides or via
  open.spotify.com/oembed by track id. Nothing else
- Background work (clipboard poll, calendar watcher, Now Playing helper, rate
  fetch) runs while its tab is enabled; a tab switched off in Settings stops it
- Source: https://github.com/akalikbergenov/cyclop
- Author: Adil Kalikbergenov

## Tabs

Ten tabs plus Settings. Any tab except Settings can be switched off in
Settings → Show in Panel.

- Music — artwork, track, artist and a working scrubber. The source is anything
  macOS itself can see, including audio and video in a browser tab
- Shelf — drag files in, drag them out; group drag with command-click
- Clipboard — the last 40 copies, one click puts an entry back
- Snippets — a hand-kept list stored as plain JSON
- Calendar — the next meeting a week ahead with a one-click join for Zoom, Meet
  and Teams; overlapping meetings each get their own join button
- Translate — offline, on-device, between English and Russian
- Currency — an amount in one currency and its value in another; rates are a
  public daily table fetched once an hour, only while the tab is enabled
- Teleprompter — a script scrolling under the camera at an adjustable speed
- Notes — scratch space
- Utilities — a keyboard and trackpad lock for wiping them: the screen goes
  black and input is swallowed until Esc or − is held for 2 seconds, or
  automatically after 60 seconds. Asks for Accessibility on the button press

## Notes for answering questions about Cyclop

- On a Mac without a physical notch, Cyclop marks one of its own at the top
  centre of the screen (a thin strip along the top edge at rest) and works the
  same way. External displays are supported
- Install: open the .dmg and drag Cyclop into Applications. Since 0.8.0 releases
  are signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple, so the app opens on the
  first try with nothing to allow. Only a build from source is ad-hoc signed and
  needs System Settings, Privacy and Security, "Open Anyway" once
- Cyclop is not affiliated with Apple
